reviews.comment: Rasmussen is by far the worst professor I have ever had at Texas A&M. He is condescending and refuses to take responsibility for his shortcomings. After taking 5 weeks to grade Exam 1, most of which were graded harshly or incorrectly, blamed students for low Exam 1 grades. Offered a retake during finals that could possibly lower your Exam 1 grade.

As an administrator, this has got to be the worst performance I've ever seen. Took them more than a month to grade the exam. Then, rather than curving had us retake the exam two days before the final. Tried to give the final during the week before finals week, which you cannot do, so they had to move the exam. Very unprofessional and condescending

All these people complaining is only because they cannot pay attention for more than 30 minutes a week. The class is not hard. Pay attention, try, do the additional work, and you will get an A. Rasmussen is a reasonable person, just be reasonable too.
Rasmussen really has no place being a professor. He is clueless on how to coordinate a class.

Taking this class during Covid was an absolute nightmare. I cannot believe the lack of understanding and cooperation from the department and Rasmussen. I am very disappointed and unsatisfied with this course. Taking this class again will be a waste of both time and money.

Absolutely awful. While the current situation has changed everything, he has done a terrible job with the 260 class. His emails are condescending, as he declines assisting those who have questions about the material. He also blames everyone's poor test performance on lack of dedication while studying.

Dr. Rasmussen is the worst professor that I have taken at Texas A&M. He royally screwed up MEEN 260 (fall 2020). They made it so the tests are online with no partial credit. Homework arbitrarily graded extremely harsh. Solution to abysmally low exam 1 avg. was to have retest during thanksgiving break the week before final exam. Hate him completely.

This prof made this class much harder than necessary. When we do bad he implies that we are not smart enough or trying enough and takes no responsibility. He assigned a second midterm 1 over break as a bonus instead of a curve like any other prof, exams have no partial credit because they are lazy to grade. Worst prof I have ever had.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Rasmussen does seem to genuinely care about students. That being said, MEEN 260 is still a lot of work, and you get the feeling that it's just kind of a mess. However, Dr. Rasmussen's office hours are very helpful, and he is pretty good at explaining confusing topics. Probably the best choice for this course.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Rasmussen is a good prof but 260 is a terrible course. It is alot of work and the weekly labs take too much time and effort. The entire course is taught through online lectures and you will have to teach yourself because there is very little that is taught or clarified in the classroom.

This course is SO much work and Professor Rasmussen likes to keep it that way. He's a decent lecturer, but there is a lot of self-teaching. In reality, the course needs to be reformed, but Rasmussen doesn't seem to care enough about his students to make that happen.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Rasmussen is the best professor that I've had at A&M so far!

This class sucks no matter who you take, but Rasmussen at least cares about imparting the knowledge you're supposed to learn in the class. He's a solid lecturer who really does care about the students, however the professor you have really doesn't matter a whole lot for this class. Be prepared for a lot of homework.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Class was really hard and a lot of work but all MEEN 260 classes have a heavy work load with the projects. He was a great professor for the class and was always open to questions.  I would take him again if I needed to.
